newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: SFE wheat steady to lower on hedging, patchy rain.
newsitem.headline: SFE wheat steady to lower on hedging, patchy rain.

text.p: Sydney Futures Exchange (SFE) wheat futures were steady to slightly weaker on Monday after patchy weekend rain in most Australian eastern grains areas.
January 1998 traded down by A$1.00 a tonne to A$192.50 on 16 lots. Settlement prices of most other untraded contracts moved in a band of plus or minus about A$1.00 a tonne.
One call option was taken out on A$200.00 January 1998 at a A$9.00 premium.
This followed continued heightened interest in Australia's drought-bound wheat market on the SYCOM overnight market on Friday with 25 trades going through at slightly weaker prices.
Hedging was taking place on both sides of the market, Phil Lindsay of Ord Minnett Jardine Fleming Futures said.
End-users and merchants were looking to buy at lower levels, believing that the sell-off would be short-lived. It was highly possible the market might head up from present levels, he said.

Some end-users were looking to buy lower protein wheat on the physical market for delivery over the next couple of months out of concern that year-end wheat would be mostly drought-affected high protein grade, he said.
This had caused buying of SFE feed grade wheat contracts. Growers remained keen sellers above A$200.00, he said.
